newsitem.title: USA: User fees would benefit bigger U.S. airlines - GAO.
newsitem.headline: User fees would benefit bigger U.S. airlines - GAO.

text.p: A proposal by larger U.S. airlines to replace the ticket tax with user fees would substantially increase the fees paid by low-fare airlines and decrease those paid by the bigger airlines, the General Accounting Office (GAO) said Monday.

"The proposal would dramatically redistribute the cost burden among airlines and could have substantial implications for domestic competition," the GAO said in a report for Congress. Under the proposal, Southwest Airlines Co would pay an extra $205 million into the Airport and Airway Trust Fund in fiscal 1997 than under the ticket tax system.
America West Airlines Inc would pay an extra $25 million under the proposed system in fiscal 1997, and other non-coalition airlines would pay a total of $312 million more, the report said.
The seven airlines that proposed the change would all benefit, the report said.

Delta Air Lines Inc would pay $140 million less, AMR Corp's American Airlines would pay $126 million less, United Airlines would pay $101 million less, USAir Group Inc would pay $88 million less, Northwest Airlines Corp would pay $78 million less, Continental Airlines Inc would pay $33 million less, and Trans World Airlines Inc would pay $27 million less.
The trust fund was established in 1970 to finance the Federal Aviation Authority's investments in the airport and airway system.
The current 10 percent ticket tax will expire after Dec. 31 this year. The FAA estimates the money in the trust fund will last until early July 1997.
